weaknesses.title: 379 visits written before the fault were lost

fixes.title: Move visits-service off its in-memory database
steps: Add a MySQL service with a named volume to the Compose file
Start visits-service with the Spring profile `mysql` (the service already ships db/mysql/schema.sql and the MySQL driver) and point SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL at it
Keep the HSQLDB profile for unit tests only
fixes.verify: python3 -m chaoslab run kill visits-service  # expect: no data-loss line, canary visit survives

verification.summary: Verified: the fix removed data_loss. Risk 8.5/10 critical before, 5.2/10 medium after; visits lost 1 before, 0 after; recovery 13.1 s before, 13.2 s after.

weaknesses.title: Owner pages returned HTTP 200 with their visits missing
weaknesses.evidence: 2 correctness probes during the fault got 200 with no visits; a status-code monitor would report everything as fine

fixes.title: Make degraded owner pages visible instead of a silent 200
fixes.why: 2 correctness probes during the fault got 200 with no visits; a status-code monitor would report everything as fine
steps: In the Gateway's owner-details fallback, mark the response as partial (for example a `X-Degraded: visits` header or a `visitsUnavailable` field)
Count fallback responses in Micrometer and alert on them, not only on 5xx
Show 'visits temporarily unavailable' in the UI rather than an empty list
fixes.verify: python3 -m chaoslab run kill visits-service  # expect: degraded pages carry the marker; the fallback counter rises

weaknesses.title: visits-service only came back because ChaosLab restarted it
weaknesses.evidence: the container has no restart policy and runs a single instance: without the experiment's undo step it would have stayed down

fixes.title: Let visits-service restart itself and run a second instance
fixes.why: the container has no restart policy and runs a single instance: without the experiment's undo step it would have stayed down
steps: Add `restart: unless-stopped` to the service in Compose (an orchestrator's liveness probe in production)
Run two instances behind Eureka so the Gateway's load balancer keeps serving while one restarts
fixes.verify: python3 -m chaoslab run kill visits-service  # with the undo step removed, expect the service back on its own

weaknesses.title: Users saw errors: up to 100% of requests failed
weaknesses.evidence: failing actions: list owners 29%, owner details 27%

fixes.title: Fail fast: lower the Gateway's 10 s TimeLimiter
fixes.why: peak p95 11000 ms against a baseline of 21 ms: callers waited for the Gateway's 10 s TimeLimiter before getting an answer
steps: In spring-petclinic-api-gateway/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/api/ApiGatewayApplication.java, defaultCustomizer sets TimeLimiterConfig timeoutDuration to 10 s; use about 2 s (well above the 20 ms normal p95)
Make it configurable (for example resilience4j.timelimiter properties) so each route can differ
Add a connect and response timeout to the Gateway's WebClient for the owner lookup, which has none
fixes.verify: python3 -m chaoslab run kill customers-service  # expect: peak p95 near 2 s instead of 10 s, throughput holds

weaknesses.title: Actions that never call the target failed too
weaknesses.evidence: list vets failed although they do not use vets-service: the failure spread through something they share, such as the Gateway's circuit breaker

fixes.title: Give each route its own circuit breaker
fixes.why: list vets failed although they do not use vets-service: the failure spread through something they share, such as the Gateway's circuit breaker
steps: In spring-petclinic-api-gateway/src/main/resources/application.yml, the default filter uses one `defaultCircuitBreaker` for every route
Name one circuit breaker per downstream service (customers, visits, vets) so one failing service cannot open the breaker for the others
fixes.verify: python3 -m chaoslab run kill vets-service  # expect: no collateral actions
